# Graph Workbench

> Graph Workbench is an open-source, graph-native workbench for governed AI workflows. It connects execution graphs with durable context graphs and packages domain workflows as installable Industry Packs.

## Start here

- [What is Graph Workbench?](https://angrykarl.github.io/graph-workbench/what-is-graph-workbench/): Product boundary, first-run journey and use cases.
- [Execution graph vs context graph](https://angrykarl.github.io/graph-workbench/execution-graph-vs-context-graph/): Why workflow control and durable organizational state are separate but connected.
- [Cross-run Agent memory](https://angrykarl.github.io/graph-workbench/cross-run-agent-memory/): How approved objects and relations become typed input to later runs.
- [Industry Packs](https://angrykarl.github.io/graph-workbench/industry-packs/): The installable unit for domain workflows, roles, tools, quality policy and context semantics.

## Primary sources

- [Source repository](https://github.com/AngryKarl/graph-workbench)
- [Architecture decision](https://github.com/AngryKarl/graph-workbench/blob/main/docs/architecture/0001-dual-graph-kernel.md)
- [Industry Pack Gallery](https://github.com/AngryKarl/graph-workbench/blob/main/docs/PACK_GALLERY.md)
- [Pack authoring guide](https://github.com/AngryKarl/graph-workbench/blob/main/docs/PACK_AUTHORING.md)
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/graph-workbench)

The Pages articles are concise discovery aids. The repository, versioned contracts and executable tests remain the authoritative sources for implementation details.
